gloss: be high, rise; lift up, exalt; take off, set apart (as a contribution)
summary: To be high and to make high: mountains, cedars and tall peoples are high, the ark rose on the flood, and Yahweh is high above all nations; a hand, a horn, a voice or a head is lifted up, and a heart lifted up is pride. The polel raises children and exalts Yahweh in praise; the hiphil lifts up a hand, a rod, a voice, a banner or the poor from the dust, and also lifts a thing off and away, the fat from the sacrifice or the crown from a king's head, and so sets a part apart for Yahweh. From that comes תְּרוּמָה, the contribution lifted off from the whole: the gifts for the tabernacle, the priests' portion, the first of the dough, and in Ezekiel the holy portion of the land; and from height comes מָרוֹם, the height, above all the heights where God dwells. Scripture's rule is that Yahweh alone is exalted, and he lifts up the lowly and brings down the proud; his servant “shall be exalted and lifted up” (Isa 52:13). Sabaic rym “raise; take away; height”, Arabic raym “excess, superiority”, Ugaritic rwm “make high”, Phoenician rm “high” and the Aramaic and Syriac rūm have the same sense.

words.gloss: be high, rise, be exalted; raise, rear, extol; lift up, exalt; lift off, take away, set apart as a contribution
words.summary: About 190 uses of the verb proper, in six stems. The brief's 88 tokens with no stem under t.bm.aa are other words filed by spelling: הָרִים “mountains” (the plural of הַר), the places Ramah and Ramoth, and the name Ram. The qal is intransitive, “be high”; the polel and hiphil make high, the polel chiefly of rearing children and of praise, the hiphil of lifting a hand, a voice or a person, and of lifting a thing off something, from which the contribution תְּרוּמָה is named.

stems.gloss: be high, tall; rise; be exalted; be lifted up; (of the heart, the eyes) be haughty

senses.definition: Of mountains, trees, stars and peoples: to be high or tall; of what was below: to rise.

evidence.note: “A people greater and taller (וָרָם) than we, cities great and walled up to heaven.”
The Emim, “a people great and many and tall (וָרָם) as the Anakim” (also Deu 2:21; 9:2).
“On the high mountains (הֶהָרִים הָרָמִים) and on the hills and under every green tree.”
“All the cedars of Lebanon, הָרָמִים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִים”; Isa 2:14, “all the high mountains”.
“From the top of the high cedar … on a high and lofty mountain I will plant it.”
“Is not God in the height of heaven? And see the head of the stars, how high they are (כִּי־רָמּוּ).”
“Lead me to the rock that is higher (יָרוּם) than I.”
“The waters increased and bore up the ark, וַתָּרָם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ”: it rose above the earth on the flood.
“The glory of Yahweh went up (וַיָּרָם) from the cherub to the threshold of the house”; the cherubim rise (Ezk 10:16–17).
Manna kept overnight וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ, “bred (raised up) worms and stank”: the one use with an object.
“Wisdom is too high (רָאמוֹת) for a fool”, spelt with א.
קוֹל רָם, “a high (loud) voice”.

senses.gloss: be high, be exalted (of Yahweh and his servant)
senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to be high above the nations and the heavens, exalted in his rule; and of his servant, to be raised up on high.

evidence.note: “רָם עַל־כָּל־גּוֹיִם יַהְוֶה, his glory above the heavens.”
“Yahweh in Zion is great, וְרָם הוּא above all the peoples.”
“Though Yahweh is high (רָם), he sees the lowly; and the proud he knows from far off.”
“I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, רָם וְנִשָּׂא.”
“Thus says רָם וְנִשָּׂא … I dwell in the height (מָרוֹם) and holy place, and with the crushed and lowly of spirit.”
“I will be exalted (אָרוּם) among the nations, I will be exalted in the earth.”
“Be exalted (רוּמָה) above the heavens, God; your glory above all the earth” (also Psa 57:12; 108:6).
“Be exalted (רוּמָה), Yahweh, in your strength.”
“Yahweh lives … and exalted (וְיָרוּם) be the God of my salvation” (2Sa 22:47).
“Therefore he will rise up (יָרוּם) to have mercy on you.”
“Behold, my servant shall act wisely; יָרוּם וְנִשָּׂא וְגָבַהּ מְאֹד”: said of the servant in the words used of Yahweh's throne (Isa 6:1; 57:15).
Balaam of Israel: “his king shall be higher (וְיָרֹם) than Agag.”

senses.gloss: be lifted up (a hand, a horn, a right hand)
senses.definition: Of a hand, arm or horn: to be raised, in power and victory.

evidence.note: “The sons of Israel were going out בְּיָד רָמָה”, with a high hand, openly and in triumph (Num 33:3).
The enemy would say, “our hand is high (יָדֵנוּ רָמָה), and Yahweh has not done all this.”
“Your hand shall be lifted up (תָּרֹם) over your adversaries.”
Hannah: “רָמָה קַרְנִי בַּיַהְוֶה”, my horn is lifted up in Yahweh.
“Strong is your hand, high (תָּרוּם) your right hand.”
Of David: “in my name his horn shall be exalted” (also Psa 89:18; 112:9).
“Yahweh, your hand is lifted up (רָמָה), they do not see.”
“The high arm (זְרוֹעַ רָמָה) is broken”: of the wicked.

senses.gloss: (of the heart, the eyes) be lifted up, haughty
senses.definition: Of a man's heart or eyes: to be lifted up in pride, above others and away from Yahweh.

evidence.note: “וְרָם לְבָבֶךָ and you forget Yahweh your God.”
The king is to read the law daily “that his heart be not lifted up (רוּם) above his brothers”.
“They were filled, וַיָּרָם לִבָּם; therefore they forgot me.”
The cedar Assyria: “its heart was lifted up in its height.”
“His heart shall be lifted up, and he shall cast down tens of thousands.”
“Yahweh, my heart is not haughty, וְלֹא־רָמוּ עֵינַי.”
Among the things Yahweh hates, עֵינַיִם רָמוֹת, haughty eyes.
“You save a humble people, but haughty eyes (וְעֵינַיִם רָמוֹת) you bring down” (2Sa 22:28).
“A generation, how lofty are its eyes!”
“A day of Yahweh of armies upon all that is proud and lofty (וָרָם).”
“The tall of stature (רָמֵי הַקּוֹמָה) hewn down, and the high brought low.”
“The wicked walk on every side, when vileness is exalted (כְּרֻם) among the sons of men.”

stems.gloss: raise, rear (children); lift up, set on high; exalt, extol (in praise)

senses.gloss: rear, bring up (children); make grow high
senses.definition: To make high by rearing: of children brought up, and of a tree made to grow tall.

evidence.note: “בָּנִים גִּדַּלְתִּי וְרוֹמַמְתִּי, and they have rebelled against me”: with גִּדֵּל, “brought up”.
Sidon: “I have not brought up young men nor reared (רוֹמַמְתִּי) virgins.”
“The waters made it great, the deep made it grow high (רֹמְמָתְהוּ).”

senses.gloss: lift up, set on high, raise up
senses.definition: To lift a person or a thing up out of danger or lowness, or to set it on high; of God's dealing with men, to exalt.

evidence.note: “Yahweh makes poor and makes rich; he brings low (מַשְׁפִּיל), he also lifts up (מְרוֹמֵם).”
“He will hide me … on a rock he will lift me up (יְרוֹמְמֵנִי).”
“You who lift me up (מְרוֹמְמִי) from the gates of death.”
“You lift me above those who rise against me” (2Sa 22:49).
“Wait for Yahweh and keep his way, וִירוֹמִמְךָ לָרֶשֶׁת אָרֶץ; when the wicked are cut off you will see it.”
Of wisdom: “exalt her (סַלְסְלֶהָ) and she will lift you up (וּתְרוֹמְמֶךָּ).”
“Righteousness exalts (תְּרוֹמֵם) a nation, but sin is a reproach to peoples.”
The storm wind “lifted up (וַתְּרוֹמֵם) its waves”.
“To raise up (לְרוֹמֵם) the house of our God and set up its ruins.”
“You have hidden their heart from understanding; therefore you will not exalt them.”
“They call him on high (אֶל־עַל); none at all lifts him up (יְרוֹמֵם).”

senses.definition: To lift Yahweh up in words: to praise him as high, beside “bless”, “praise”, “magnify”.

evidence.note: “This is my God and I will glorify him, my father's God, וַאֲרֹמְמֶנְהוּ.”
“Magnify (גַּדְּלוּ) Yahweh with me, and let us exalt (וּנְרוֹמְמָה) his name together.”
“I will extol you (אֲרוֹמִמְךָ), Yahweh, for you have drawn me up.”
“Exalt (רוֹמְמוּ) Yahweh our God, and bow down at his footstool” (also Psa 99:9).
“Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people.”
“You are my God, and I will praise you; my God, I will exalt you.”
“I will exalt you, my God the King, and bless your name forever.”
“Yahweh, you are my God; I will exalt you, I will praise your name.”

senses.definition: The passive of the polel: of the horns of the righteous, of Yahweh's name and right hand.

evidence.note: “All the horns of the wicked I will cut off; the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up (תְּרוֹמַמְנָה).”
“Blessed be your glorious name, which is exalted (וּמְרוֹמַם) above all blessing and praise.”
“The right hand of Yahweh is exalted (רוֹמֵמָה).”

senses.definition: To raise oneself up: of Yahweh rising to act, and of a king who sets himself above every god.

evidence.note: “Now I will arise (אָקוּם), says Yahweh; now I will exalt myself (אֵרוֹמָם); now I will be lifted up.”
“The king shall do as he wills, וְיִתְרוֹמֵם וְיִתְגַּדֵּל over every god.”
Paul's “who opposes and exalts himself above all that is called God”, after Dan 11:36.

stems.gloss: raise, lift up; exalt; lift off, take up, take away; raise (a contribution), set apart, present

senses.gloss: raise, lift up (a hand, rod, voice, head, horn, banner)
senses.definition: To lift something up: a hand in an oath or against someone, a rod, the voice, the head, the horn, a banner, a stone.

evidence.note: Abram: “הֲרִמֹתִי יָדִי to Yahweh, God Most High”: the hand lifted in an oath.
“He raised (וַיָּרֶם) his right hand and his left hand to heaven and swore by him who lives forever”; Rev 10:5–6.
The messenger “lifted up his hand to heaven and swore”, after Dan 12:7.
“When Moses lifted up (יָרִים) his hand, Israel prevailed.”
“Lift up (הָרֵם) your rod and stretch out your hand over the sea.”
“He lifted up the rod and struck the waters.”
Jeroboam “lifted up his hand against the king” (1Ki 11:27).
“Without you no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”
“When he heard that I raised (הֲרִימֹתִי) my voice and cried.”
“Lift up (הָרִימִי) your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem.”
“Lift up your voice like a shofar.”
Many “shouted aloud (לְהָרִים קוֹל) for joy”.
“Lift up (הָרִימוּ) a voice to them”; a banner, Isa 49:22; 62:10.
“I will lift up my hand to the nations and set up (אָרִים) my banner to the peoples.”
“You, Yahweh, are a shield about me, my glory, וּמֵרִים רֹאשִׁי.”
“He shall drink of the brook by the way; therefore he shall lift up (יָרִים) the head.”
“To the wicked, Do not lift up the horn; do not lift up your horn on high” (Psa 75:5–6).
“He will give strength to his king, וְיָרֵם קֶרֶן מְשִׁיחוֹ.”
“He has lifted up (וַיָּרֶם) a horn for his people.”
“You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries.”
“He has exalted the horn of your adversaries.”
“Lift up (וְהָרִימוּ) each man a stone on his shoulder.”
“Jacob took a stone and set it up (וַיְרִימֶהָ) as a pillar.”

senses.gloss: exalt, raise (a person) to a high place
senses.definition: Of God: to raise a man from lowness to rule or honour; of a man: to set himself or his throne on high.

evidence.note: “He raises the poor from the dust, from the ash heap יָרִים אֶבְיוֹן, to seat them with princes” (Psa 113:7).
“God is judge: he puts down (יַשְׁפִּיל) one and lifts up (יָרִים) another.”
“I have exalted (הֲרִימוֹתִי) one chosen out of the people; I have found David my servant.”
To Jeroboam: “I exalted you from among the people and made you leader over my people Israel.”
To Baasha: “I exalted you out of the dust.”
The king of Babylon: “Above the stars of God I will exalt (אָרִים) my throne.”
“The wise shall inherit glory, but fools מֵרִים קָלוֹן”: shame is what they carry off.
In the same verse: “exalt (הַגְבֵּהַּ) the low and bring low the high”, with another verb.

senses.gloss: lift off, take up, take away
senses.definition: To lift a thing up off where it is: the fat off a sacrifice, the ashes off the altar, a cloak or axe-head off the ground, a stumbling block off the road, the crown off a head.

evidence.note: “All the fat of the bull of the sin offering he shall lift off (יָרִים) from it” (also Lev 4:19).
“The priest shall take up (וְהֵרִים) from the grain offering its memorial.”
“He shall take up (וְהֵרִים) the ashes … and put them beside the altar.”
“He took up (וַיָּרֶם) the cloak of Elijah that had fallen from him.”
“Take it up (הָרֶם לָךְ)”: the axe-head floating on the water.
“Prepare the way, הָרִימוּ מִכְשׁוֹל מִדֶּרֶךְ עַמִּי”: take the stumbling block up out of the way.
“Put away violence … take away (הָרִימוּ) your evictions from my people.”
“Remove the turban, וְהָרֵים הָעֲטָרָה”: take off the crown.

senses.gloss: raise (a contribution), set apart, present (to Yahweh)
senses.definition: To lift off part of what one has, of produce, tithe, spoil or land, and set it apart for Yahweh, the priests or the sanctuary; and so to present or give.

evidence.note: “When you eat of the bread of the land, you shall raise (תָּרִימוּ) a contribution (תְרוּמָה) to Yahweh.”
“Of the first of your dough you shall raise a cake as a contribution; as the contribution of the threshing floor, so you shall raise it.”
To the Levites: “you shall raise from it a contribution of Yahweh, a tenth of the tithe” (Num 18:24–32).
“Of all your gifts you shall raise every contribution of Yahweh, of all its best, its holy part, from it.”
“Raise (וַהֲרֵמֹתָ) a levy for Yahweh from the men of war”: one in five hundred of the spoil.
“The holy things of the sons of Israel, which they raise to Yahweh.”
“Everyone who raised a contribution of silver and bronze brought Yahweh's contribution.”
“When you divide the land by lot for an inheritance, you shall raise a contribution to Yahweh, a holy portion of the land.”
“The contribution which you shall raise”, 25,000 broad (also Ezk 45:13; 48:9, 20).
“The contribution of the house of our God, which the king and his counsellors … had raised (הֵרִימוּ).”
“Josiah gave (וַיָּרֶם) to the people lambs and kids”; his princes likewise (2Ch 35:8–9; 30:24).

stems.gloss: be lifted off, be taken away

senses.definition: The passive of the hiphil's “lift off”: of a sacrifice's portion lifted off, and of the continual offering taken away.

evidence.note: “As it is lifted off (יוּרַם) from the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings.”
“The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, which was waved and which was lifted off (הוּרָם).”
“By him the continual was taken away (הוּרַם, written הרים)”: the form is read as a hophal.

evidence.locator: Isa.52.13, יָרוּם → ὑψωθήσεται; 1Sa.2.10, וְיָרֵם → ὑψώσει; Psa.37.34, וִירוֹמִמְךָ → ὑψώσει; Psa.75.11 → ὑψωθήσεται; ὑψόω renders רוּם ×31

evidence.note: Mary, after Hannah (1Sa 2:7–8): “he has put down the mighty from their thrones and exalted (ὕψωσεν) the lowly.”
“Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted” (Luk 14:11; 18:14).
“As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up (ὑψωθῆναι).”
“And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all to me”; “this he said, signifying by what death he would die” (Jhn 12:33).
“Being exalted (ὑψωθείς) by the right hand of God.”
“Him God exalted with his right hand to be Prince and Saviour.”
“He exalted the people … and with a high arm brought them out”: the high hand of Exo 14:8.
“Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you.”
“Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time.”

evidence.locator: Isa.6.1, רָם → ὑψηλοῦ; Psa.113.4; 138.6, רָם → ὑψηλός; Exo.14.8 בְּיָד רָמָה; ὑψηλός renders רוּם ×11

evidence.note: μετὰ βραχίονος ὑψηλοῦ, “with a high arm”.
“What is high (ὑψηλόν) among men is an abomination before God.”
A high priest “made higher than the heavens”.
“Sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high (ἐν ὑψηλοῖς).”

evidence.locator: Exo.7.20, וַיָּרֶם → ἐπάρας; Exo.17.11, יָרִים → ἐπῆρεν; Num.20.11 → ἐπάρας

evidence.note: “He lifted up (ἐπάρας) his hands and blessed them.”
“Lifting up holy hands without wrath and doubting.”
Peter “lifted up his voice”: הֵרִים קוֹל.

evidence.locator: Ezk.45.1, 13; 48.9, 20, תָּרִימוּ → ἀφοριεῖτε, ἀφοριοῦσι; Num.18.24, יָרִימוּ → ἀφορίσωσιν

evidence.note: “Set apart (ἀφορίσατε) for me Barnabas and Saul for the work.”
“Set apart for the gospel of God.”

parallels.note: “Lift up, be lifted up”: the fixed partner, רָם וְנִשָּׂא, of Yahweh's throne and of the servant.
“Be high, be haughty”: the same height and the same pride.
Piel “bring up, magnify”: beside the polel in rearing and in praise.
“Arise”: Yahweh's rising to act, beside his exalting himself.

opposites.note: “Be low; (hiphil) bring low”: what Yahweh does to the high, as he lifts up the low.

phrases.gloss: with a high hand: openly, defiantly; of Israel leaving Egypt, and of the sin done in defiance of Yahweh

evidence.note: “The soul that does anything with a high hand … reviles Yahweh, and that soul shall be cut off.”

phrases.gloss: lift up the hand: in an oath, or against someone
lift up the voice: cry out, proclaim, sing aloud
lift up the horn: give strength and victory; (of the wicked) behave arrogantly

evidence.note: Heman's sons, “in the words of God, to lift up the horn”.

phrases.gloss: the heart is lifted up: pride that forgets Yahweh
lift up the head: restore, vindicate

words.gloss: contribution, what is lifted off and set apart (for Yahweh)
words.summary: The noun of the hiphil “lift off, set apart”, 76 times: a part taken off from the whole and given to Yahweh, nearly always with the verb (תָּרִימוּ תְרוּמָה, “raise a contribution”). It is given from the heart for the tabernacle, levied as the half-shekel, taken off the sacrifices for the priests, from the first of the dough and the tithe, from spoil, and in Ezekiel from the land itself. Beside it stands תְּנוּפָה, the wave offering (Exo 29:27).

senses.definition: What the people set apart and bring for Yahweh's house and its work: freely given for the tabernacle, levied as the half-shekel of atonement, given again for the house in Ezra's day.

evidence.note: “That they take for me a contribution; from every man whose heart moves him you shall take my contribution.”
“Gold and silver and bronze, blue and purple …” (Exo 25:3–7).
“Take from among you a contribution to Yahweh; whoever is of a willing heart, let him bring it.”
“Everyone whose heart lifted him up … brought Yahweh's contribution for the work of the tent of meeting.”
“Let no man or woman do more work for the contribution of the sanctuary”: the people brought too much.
“Half a shekel … a contribution to Yahweh”, given by rich and poor alike “to atone for your souls” (Exo 30:13–15).
“The contribution of the house of our God.”
“He who is too poor for a contribution chooses a tree that will not rot”: to make an idol.

senses.gloss: the priests' portion; the holy gifts given to the priests and Levites
senses.definition: What is lifted off from the people's offerings and produce and given to the priests and Levites: the thigh of the peace offering, the first of the dough, the tithe and the tenth of the tithe, the holy things.

evidence.note: “The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution I have taken … and given them to Aaron the priest and his sons.”
“It is a contribution, and a contribution it shall be from the sons of Israel … their contribution to Yahweh.”
“The breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you shall eat in a clean place.”
“I have given you charge of my contributions, all the holy things of the sons of Israel.”
“All the contributions of the holy things … a covenant of salt forever.”
“Of the first of your dough you shall raise a cake as a contribution”; Rom 11:16.
“If the firstfruit is holy, the lump is also”: the dough-offering of Num 15:20–21.
“The tithe of the sons of Israel, which they raise to Yahweh as a contribution, I have given to the Levites.”
“Your tithes and the contribution of your hand” are brought to the place Yahweh chooses (Deu 12:11, 17).
A priest's daughter married to a stranger “shall not eat of the contribution of the holy things”.
“Every contribution of every kind … shall be the priests'.”
“The first of our dough and our contributions” brought to the chambers of the house of God.
Under Hezekiah: “they faithfully brought in the contribution and the tithes and the holy things.”
“Will a man rob God? Yet you rob me. But you say, How have we robbed you? בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר וְהַתְּרוּמָה.”
From the spoil of Midian, “Yahweh's contribution” to Eleazar the priest (Num 31:41, 52).

senses.gloss: the holy contribution of the land (in Ezekiel)
senses.definition: In Ezekiel's division of the land, the square portion set apart from the whole for Yahweh: the priests' land with the sanctuary in its midst, the Levites' land, and the city's.

evidence.note: “You shall raise a contribution to Yahweh, a holy portion of the land, 25,000 long and 10,000 broad.”
“For these shall be the holy contribution: for the priests … and the sanctuary of Yahweh shall be in its midst.”
“All the contribution shall be 25,000 by 25,000: you shall raise it four-square, the holy contribution with the possession of the city.”
“In my holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel … there all the house of Israel shall serve me in the land; there I will require your contributions.”

senses.definition: In a ruler's hands, what he takes off the people for himself.

evidence.note: “A king by justice establishes the land, וְאִישׁ תְּרוּמוֹת tears it down”: the man of exactions.
“This is the contribution you shall raise”: the prince's due fixed by measure (Ezk 45:13–16), against the exactions of Ezk 45:9.

senses.definition: David's lament for Gilboa: fields whose produce would be lifted off as offerings.

evidence.note: “Mountains of Gilboa, no dew nor rain on you, וּשְׂדֵי תְרוּמֹת.”

evidence.locator: Exo.25.2, תְּרוּמָה → ἀπαρχάς; Num.18.8, תְּרוּמֹתָי → ἀπαρχῶν; ἀπαρχή renders תְּרוּמָה ×20; in Num.15.20–21 it renders רֵאשִׁית

evidence.note: “If the firstfruit (ἀπαρχή) is holy, the lump is also”: the first of the dough raised as a contribution (Num 15:20–21).
“Christ is risen from the dead, the firstfruit of those who sleep.”
“That we should be a kind of firstfruit of his creatures.”
“Redeemed from among men, firstfruit to God and to the Lamb.”

parallels.note: The wave offering: the breast waved, the thigh lifted off.
The tithe, named with the contribution.

phrases.gloss: the thigh of the contribution: the priest's portion of the peace offering

words.gloss: height, high place; on high (heaven); haughtily
words.summary: The place that is high, 54 times, mostly in poetry: the heights of the field, of the city, of a rock, of the mountain of Israel; and above all “the height”, the heaven where Yahweh dwells, from which he looks down and sends. Used as an adverb it is “on high”, and of men's speech or bearing “haughtily”.

senses.definition: A high place on the earth: a hill or ridge, the top of a city, a dwelling cut high in the rock; “the mountain of the height of Israel”.

evidence.note: “Naphtali on the heights (מְרוֹמֵי) of the field.”
Wisdom “calls on the tops of the heights of the city” (Pro 8:2; 9:14).
Shebna “hewing his grave on high, carving a dwelling for himself in the rock”.
Edom, “dwelling in the clefts of the rock, מְרוֹם שִׁבְתּוֹ” (Jer 49:16).
“To set his nest on high (בַּמָּרוֹם).”
“On the mountain of the height of Israel (בְּהַר מְרוֹם יִשְׂרָאֵל) I will plant it”: the twig taken from the top of the cedar.
“On the mountains of the height of Israel shall be their fold.”
“They shall come and sing on the height of Zion.”
Sennacherib: “I have come up to the height of the mountains” (Isa 37:24).
“He brings down the dwellers on high, the lofty city.”
The ostrich “lifts herself on high”.

senses.gloss: the height, on high: heaven, where God dwells
senses.definition: The height above the earth, heaven, the place of Yahweh's throne and dwelling, from which he looks down, sends and acts; with מִן, “from on high”.

evidence.note: “I dwell in the height (מָרוֹם) and the holy place, and with the crushed and lowly of spirit.”
“He looked down from the height of his holiness; from heaven (מִשָּׁמַיִם) Yahweh beheld the earth.”
“Mightier than the noise of many waters … is Yahweh on high.”
“You, Yahweh, are on high forever.”
“Yahweh will roar from on high.”
“A glorious throne, on high from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.”
“Praise Yahweh from the heavens, praise him in the heights (בַּמְּרוֹמִים).”
“Even now my witness is in heaven, and my advocate in the heights.”
“He makes peace in his heights.”
“He sent from on high, he took me” (Psa 18:17; 144:7).
“Until the spirit is poured upon us from on high (מִמָּרוֹם), and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field.”
“Yahweh will punish the host of the height in the height, and the kings of the earth on the earth”: the rulers set on high.
“The windows from on high are opened, and the foundations of the earth shake”: as at the flood (Gen 7:11).
“Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these?”
“Shall I bow myself before God on high?”
“From on high he sent fire into my bones.”
“You have gone up to the height (לַמָּרוֹם), you have led captivity captive, you have received gifts among men”; Eph 4:8.
Paul quotes Psa 68:19 of Christ: “having gone up on high (εἰς ὕψος)”.
“Over it return on high.”
“To set the lowly on high (לְמָרוֹם), and those who mourn are lifted to safety.”

senses.definition: As an adverb of speech or bearing: loftily, proudly; and of men, the high places of rank.

evidence.note: “They speak oppression from on high (מִמָּרוֹם)”, loftily.
“Many fight against me proudly (מָרוֹם).”
“You have lifted up your eyes on high, against the Holy One of Israel” (2Ki 19:22).
“Folly is set in great heights (בַּמְּרוֹמִים), and the rich sit low.”
“Your judgments are on high, out of his sight.”

evidence.locator: Psa.68.19, לַמָּרוֹם → εἰς ὕψος; Isa.40.26; Psa.102.20; ὕψος renders מָרוֹם ×19

evidence.note: “Having gone up on high (εἰς ὕψος) he led captivity captive”: Psa 68:19.
“Stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high (ἐξ ὕψους)”: the spirit from on high of Isa 32:15.
“The dayspring from on high has visited us.”
“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in his exaltation (ὕψει).”

evidence.locator: Psa.148.1, בַּמְּרוֹמִים → ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις; Job.16.19 → ἐν ὑψίστοις; ὕψιστος renders מָרוֹם ×5

evidence.note: “Glory to God in the highest (ἐν ὑψίστοις), and on earth peace.”
“Hosanna in the highest.”

words.summary: The verbal noun, six times: the height of the heavens, and, of the heart or eyes, haughtiness.

senses.definition: Height, as of the heavens against the depth of the earth.

evidence.note: “The heavens for height (לָרוּם) and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings is unsearchable.”

senses.gloss: haughtiness, loftiness (of men, of heart and eyes)
senses.definition: The heart or eyes lifted up: pride, which Yahweh brings low.

evidence.note: “The lofty eyes of man shall be humbled, וְשַׁח רוּם אֲנָשִׁים, and Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day.”
The same refrain.
“I will punish the fruit of the greatness of heart of the king of Assyria, and the glory of רוּם עֵינָיו.”
“The pride of Moab … his loftiness and his pride and his arrogance and וְרֻם לִבּוֹ.”
“רוּם־עֵינַיִם and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, are sin.”

words.summary: The feminine of the participle רָם, “a high (place)”. As a common noun it is clear only in Ezekiel 16, the raised platforms Jerusalem built at every street-head for her harlotries; elsewhere it is the name Ramah, “the height” (most of the 26 tokens under t.bm.ag are the place), and at 1Sa 22:6 either. The places are left out; see the note.

senses.definition: A raised place built in the open street for idolatrous rites, beside the גַּב “mound”.

evidence.note: “You built yourself a mound (גָּב) and made yourself a רָמָה in every square.”
“At every head of the way you built your רָמָה.”
“They shall throw down your mound and break down your platforms (רָמֹתַיִךְ).”
Saul sat “under the tamarisk בָּרָמָה”: “on the height”, or “in Ramah”.

words.summary: Twice, the noun of the polel “extol”.

senses.definition: The lifting up of God in words of praise.

evidence.note: “The high praises (רוֹמְמוֹת) of God in their throat, and a two-edged sword in their hand.”
“I cried to him with my mouth, וְרוֹמַם was under my tongue.”

senses.definition: Upward, on high.

evidence.note: “The deep gave its voice, רוֹם יָדֵיהוּ נָשָׂא”: it lifted its hands on high.

senses.definition: Walking with the neck held high, in pride.

evidence.note: “An evil from which you shall not remove your necks, וְלֹא תֵלְכוּ רוֹמָה, for it is an evil time.”

words.summary: Once, the noun of the polel; the same passage has the hithpolel אֵרוֹמָם (Isa 33:10).

senses.definition: Yahweh's lifting himself up to act, before which the nations scatter.

evidence.note: “At the noise of the tumult the peoples fled; מֵרוֹמְמֻתֶךָ the nations were scattered.”
“Now I will exalt myself (אֵרוֹמָם).”

words.summary: Once, of Pharaoh's carcass filling the valleys. Formed as an abstract “height” of the root, it seems to mean the high heap of his corpse (or his lofty stature brought down), but one verse does not fix it; the link to the root's sense rests on the form alone.

senses.definition: What is piled high: the body of the great dragon spread over mountains and valleys.

evidence.note: “I will lay your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with רָמוּתֶךָ.”

words.gloss: special contribution, portion set apart (from the contribution)
words.summary: Once, a noun formed from תְּרוּמָה: the Levites' part set apart within the holy contribution of the land.

words.gloss: be lifted up; (aphel) lift up, exalt; (pael) extol; (hithpaal) lift oneself up
words.summary: Daniel's Aramaic, four times, all of Nebuchadnezzar and Belshazzar: the king whose heart was lifted up was brought down, until he extolled the King of heaven. The pael and hithpaal are the polel forms מְרוֹמֵם and הִתְרוֹמַמְתָּ. BDB's key xt.ah.aa also counts Exo 15:23 מָרִים “bitter” by spelling.

senses.definition: Of the heart: to be lifted up, in pride against God.

evidence.note: “When his heart was lifted up (רִם לִבְבֵהּ) and his spirit hardened to act proudly, he was deposed from his kingly throne.”

senses.definition: To raise a man to high place, the opposite of humbling him.

evidence.note: “Whom he would he raised up (מָרִים), and whom he would he put down (מַשְׁפִּל).”

senses.definition: To praise God as high.

evidence.note: “Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise וּמְרוֹמֵם and honour the King of heaven … and those who walk in pride he is able to humble.”

senses.definition: To set oneself up against God.

evidence.note: “You have lifted yourself up (הִתְרוֹמַמְתָּ) against the Lord of heaven.”

senses.definition: The height of an image, a tree or a house.

evidence.note: The image of gold, “רוּמֵהּ sixty cubits, its breadth six cubits”.
The house of God: “רוּמֵהּ sixty cubits, its breadth sixty cubits.”
“A tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was great.”
“Its height reached to heaven” (Dan 4:17).

words.gloss: (aphel) lift up, raise, exalt; (ettaphal) be lifted up, be exalted, exalt oneself; (palpel) exalt; (ethpalpal) be magnified
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܪܡ, about 58 times in the New Testament, for ὑψόω, ἐπαίρω and ὑπερυψόω: lifting up eyes, voice and hands, God exalting the lowly and his Son, and the Son of man lifted up.

senses.definition: To raise the eyes, the voice, the hands or the head.

evidence.note: “וַארִים his hands and blessed them.”
“Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven.”
The tax collector “would not even lift up (נרִים) his eyes to heaven”.
“Look up and lift up your heads, for your redemption draws near.”
Peter “lifted up his voice”.
“Lifting up (מרִימִין) clean hands.”
The messenger “lifted up (דַּארִים) his hand to heaven” and swore: Dan 12:7.

senses.definition: Of God: to raise up the lowly, Israel, and Jesus.

evidence.note: “He has put down the mighty from their seats, וַארִים the lowly.”
“Him God has made head and saviour וַארִימֵה by his right hand.”
“He exalted the people … and with a high (רָמָא) arm brought them out.”
“Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you (תּרִימכֻֿון) in due time.”
“Whoever exalts himself (דַּנרִים נַפשֵׁה) will be humbled.”

stems.gloss: be lifted up, be exalted; exalt oneself

senses.gloss: be lifted up, be exalted; be proud
senses.definition: To be raised on high, of the Son of man and of the humble; and, reflexively, to raise oneself up in pride.

evidence.note: “So must the Son of man be lifted up (למֵתּתּרָמֻו).”
“When I am lifted up (דֵּאתּתּרִימֵתֿ) from the earth I will draw everyone to me” (Jhn 12:34).
“He is exalted (אֵתּתּרִים) by the right hand of God.”
“Whoever humbles himself shall be exalted (נֵתּתּרִים)” (Luk 14:11; 18:14).
“Do not be high-minded (תֵּתּרִים), but fear.”
“Lest I should be exalted above measure.”
“Lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the false accuser.”

senses.definition: God's raising on high.

evidence.note: “Therefore God has highly exalted him (רַמרמֵה) and given him a name above every name”, for ὑπερύψωσεν.
“Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will exalt you (וַנרַמרֵמכֻֿון).”

evidence.note: “The name of the Lord Jesus was magnified (וּמֵתֿרַמרַם).”

words.summary: The participle-adjective of the Peshitta, as Hebrew רָם: a high mountain, a loud voice, a high arm, and the proud.

senses.definition: Of a mountain or wall: high.

evidence.note: “He brought them up into a high mountain (לטֻורָא רָמָא).”
“A great and high mountain”; its wall “great and high” (Rev 21:12).

senses.definition: Of the voice: high, loud, as קוֹל רָם.

evidence.note: “Jesus cried with a loud (רָמָא) voice.”

senses.gloss: high, proud; what is high among men
senses.definition: Of men and their esteem: high, proud.

evidence.note: “God resists the proud (לרָמֵא) and gives grace to the humble.”
“What is high (דּרָם) among men is an abomination before God.”
Men “proud (רָמֵא)”.

senses.definition: Height, and the height of heaven from which God sends.

evidence.note: “The dayspring from on high (מֵן רַומָא) has visited us.”
“Until you are clothed with power from on high (מֵן רַומָא).”
“The breadth and length and depth and height.”
“Nor height nor depth.”

“Casting down every high thing (רַומָא) that exalts itself against the knowledge of God.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's form of מָרוֹם, for ὕψιστος and ὑψηλός of the heavens.

senses.definition: The heights of heaven.

evidence.note: “Glory to God בַּמרַומֵא, and on earth peace.”
“Hosanna בַּמרַומֵא” (Mrk 11:10; Luk 19:38).
“He went up לַמרַומָא and led captivity captive”: Psa 68:19 לַמָּרוֹם.

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for βουνός, the form of Hebrew רָמָה; also the name Ramah/Arimathea.

senses.definition: A hill, a height.

cognates.gloss: (Sabaic) make higher, raise; take away; height, upward; exalted (of a god); (mrym) top, roof
cognates.note: Old South Arabian keeps both sides of the Hebrew: raising a wall, a god called “the Exalted”, height in cubits, and also “take away” (the hiphil's “lift off”); mrym “top, roof” is the form of מָרוֹם. Sabaic has y where Hebrew has w in the middle of the root.

evidence.locator: p. 487, RYM
evidence.note: “MAKE HIGHER, RAISE … C448/2: wstw wrymw kl gnʾhw ‘they enlarged and raised all its wall’”; “TAKE AWAY … ‘they took away the booty (?)’”; “HEIGHT; adv = rymm: UPWARD, HIGHER … ‘thirty-five cubits (in) height’”; “adj: EXALTED, in divine epithets”; mrym “TOP, HIGHEST POINT; ROOF or TERRACE of a building … ‘from its roof to its foundation’”.

cognates.gloss: excess, superiority; (Yemen) a flight of stairs; small mountains; (rayyama) exceed
cognates.note: What rises above another: Lane's raym is “excess, or superiority” (“this has raym over this”), in the speech of Yemen “stairs” (“ascend the raym”) and “small mountains”; the verb is to exceed another. Arabic has y in the middle of the root, as Sabaic and Geʿez.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1204, art. ريم, رَيْمٌ (n17304)
evidence.note: “Excess, redundance, or superiority … i. q. دَرَجَةٌ [A series of stairs] of the dial. of El-Yemen … اُسْمُكْ فِى الرَّيْمِ, meaning اِصْعَدِ الدَّرَجَةِ [Ascend thou the stairs] … And Small mountains.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1204, art. ريم, ريّم عَلَيْهِ (n17303)
evidence.note: “He exceeded him … in journeying, or pace, and the like.”

cognates.gloss: go away, depart from, quit (a place)
cognates.note: Biella compares it with Sabaic rym “take away”; if the two belong together it is the hiphil's “lift off, take away” (Isa 57:14; Ezk 21:31) seen from the other side. Whether it is the same root as raym “excess” is not shown.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1203, art. ريم, رَيْمٌ (n17302)
evidence.note: “The verb is رَامَ, aor. يَرِيمُ, [He went away, or departed; and he quitted a place …] … mostly used in negative phrases.”

Proto-Semitic *rayam-, descendants
evidence.note: Lists Geʿez ረየመ (räyämä) with Hebrew רָם, Aramaic רָם, Syriac ܪܳܡ, Sabaic rym and Ugaritic rm.

doctrine.statement: Hannah: “Yahweh makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, he also lifts up (מְרוֹמֵם). He raises the poor from the dust, from the ash heap he lifts up the needy, to seat them with princes” (1Sa 2:7–8; Psa 113:7–8). “God is judge: he puts down one and lifts up another” (Psa 75:8); he “sets the lowly on high” (Job 5:11). Against this, “the haughtiness of men shall be brought low, and Yahweh alone shall be exalted in that day” (Isa 2:11, 17); the king's heart must not be lifted up above his brothers (Deu 17:20), and when Israel's heart was lifted up they forgot Yahweh (Deu 8:14; Hos 13:6). Mary takes up Hannah's words, “he has put down the mighty from their thrones and exalted the lowly” (Luk 1:52), and Jesus gives it as a rule: “whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted” (Mat 23:12; Luk 14:11; 18:14); “humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time” (1Pe 5:6; Jas 4:10). The psalm says when and where: “wait for Yahweh and keep his way, and he will exalt you to inherit the land; when the wicked are cut off you will see it” (Psa 37:34), the inheritance Jesus promised the meek (Mat 5:5, from Psa 37:11). From the verses: exaltation is God's to give, not a man's to take; he gives it to those who humble themselves, and its full measure is still to come, when the wicked are cut off and the meek inherit the land.

Yahweh says of his servant, “he shall be exalted (יָרוּם) and lifted up and be very high” (Isa 52:13), in the words used of Yahweh's own throne (Isa 6:1; 57:15); and the same passage goes on to his marred face, his being cut off from the land of the living, and his grave with the wicked (Isa 52:14; 53:8–9, 12). Jesus spoke of his death with the same word: “as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of man be lifted up” (Jhn 3:14); “when you have lifted up the Son of man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself” (Jhn 8:28); “I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all to me”, which John explains, “this he said, signifying by what death he would die” (Jhn 12:32–33). After the resurrection Peter says, “this Jesus God raised up … being exalted by the right hand of God … God has made him both Lord and Christ” (Act 2:32–33, 36), and “him God exalted with his right hand to be Prince and Saviour” (Act 5:31). Paul: “he humbled himself, becoming obedient to death, the death of the cross; therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name above every name … to the glory of God the Father” (Php 2:8–11). So in the psalm Yahweh says of David, “I have exalted one chosen out of the people” (Psa 89:20), and Hannah's song ends, “he will exalt the horn of his anointed” (1Sa 2:10). From the verses: the one exalted is a man chosen out of the people, lifted up first on the cross and then by God to his right hand; the exaltation is God's act and God's gift to him, given because he was obedient to death, and it is to the glory of God the Father.

Ezekiel's word to Zedekiah: “you, profane wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come … Thus says the Lord Yahweh: Remove the turban and take off (וְהָרֵים) the crown; this shall not be as it was; exalt the low and bring low the high. Overturned, overturned, overturned I will make it; this also shall be no more, until he comes whose right it is, and I will give it to him” (Ezk 21:30–32). Zedekiah's sons were slain before his eyes and he was taken blind to Babylon (2Ki 25:6–7), and no son of David has reigned in Jerusalem since. “Until he comes whose right it is” answers Jacob's “the sceptre shall not depart from Judah … until Shiloh comes, and to him shall be the obedience of the peoples” (Gen 49:10). The messenger told Mary of her son, “the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever” (Luk 1:32–33), and the apostles asked the risen Jesus, “will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”, a question he did not deny but answered as to its time (Act 1:6–7). From the verses: the crown of David's kingdom was lifted off and the kingdom overturned, to stay so until the Messiah comes; then God will give it to him, on David's throne over the house of Jacob.

When the land is divided again among the tribes, Ezekiel is told, “you shall raise (תָּרִימוּ) a contribution (תְּרוּמָה) to Yahweh, a holy portion of the land” (Ezk 45:1): a square of 25,000 cubits lifted off from the whole as the first of the dough is lifted off from the dough (Num 15:20), holding the priests' portion with “the sanctuary of Yahweh in its midst”, the Levites' portion, and the city's, with the prince's land on either side (Ezk 48:8–22). The twelve tribes have their portions from north to south (Ezk 48:1–7, 23–29), and the city's name from that day is “Yahweh is there” (Ezk 48:35). Earlier: “in my holy mountain, in the mountain of the height of Israel … there all the house of Israel, all of them, shall serve me in the land; there I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions … when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land which I lifted my hand to give to your fathers” (Ezk 20:40–42). This division has never yet been made: those who came back from Babylon were a remnant who lived in the cities of Judah and Benjamin (Ezr 2:1, 64; Neh 11:1–4, 20). From the verses: the land sworn to the fathers is still to be divided to all Israel gathered into it, and from it a holy contribution, with Yahweh's sanctuary in its midst, will be set apart to him.

Isaiah looks for the change of land and people “until the spirit is poured upon us from on high (מִמָּרוֹם), and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field” (Isa 32:15); “I will pour water on the thirsty … I will pour my spirit on your seed” (Isa 44:3). Jesus told the disciples, “stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high” (Luk 24:49), and “you will receive power when the holy spirit has come upon you” (Act 1:8); Peter said of the risen Jesus, “being exalted by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the holy spirit, he has poured out this which you see and hear” (Act 2:33). From the verses: the spirit from on high is spoken of as power that clothes men and is poured out like water, sent from the Father where he dwells: it is God's power, not another person beside him.

note: Root key רומ, the brief's. BDB keys claimed: t.bm.aa (verb), t.bm.as, t.bm.ar, t.bm.ab, t.bm.ag, t.bm.an, t.bm.ac, t.bm.ae, t.bm.ao, t.bm.am, t.bm.at, and the Aramaic xt.ah.aa, xt.ah.ab. Counts are inflated by spelling: t.bm.aa has 88 no-stem tokens that are הָרִים “mountains” (הַר, e.cf.ab), the places Ramah/Ramoth and the name Ram; t.bm.ag (26) is mostly the place Ramah; xt.ah.aa counts Exo 15:23 מָרִים “bitter”. The brief leaves out Exo 15:1, 21 (רָמָה “he has thrown”, root רמה, rightly) and Num 15:30 בְּיָד רָמָה (wrongly: it is the qal participle of this root, cited under the phrase). Not in the brief's stem lists but cited: Psa 118:16 רוֹמֵמָה (polal), Dan 8:11 הוּרַם (hophal, Ketiv הרים). The brief's “Poel” (Ezr 9:9) is the polel. Biblical Aramaic מְרוֹמֵם (Dan 4:34) and הִתְרוֹמַמְתָּ (Dan 5:23) are polel forms, filed under “pael” and “hithpaal” because the schema has no Aramaic polel. Left out as place names, which cannot be name entries: רָמָה Ramah (t.bm.ah; Mat 2:18 quotes Jer 31:15), רָמוֹת/רָאמוֹת Ramoth (t.bm.ak, whose tokens are mostly נֶגֶב filed by mistake; Job 28:18 רָאמוֹת “coral” is another word), רָמַת Ramath (t.bm.aj), רוּמָה Rumah (t.bm.ad), רֶמֶת Remeth (t.bm.aq), the gentilic רָמָתִי (t.bm.ai), and the zero-token cross-references t.bm.al, t.cu.ad, t.cx.ae, t.cx.am, t.da.ad, t.dc.ac, w.bq.ak, m.dk.ai. The niphal-like וַיֵּרֹמּוּ (Ezk 10:15, 17, 19) and הֵרֹמּוּ (Num 17:10) belong to רמם and are left there. Names: name entries written for Ram, Romamti-ezer, Abiram, Ahiram, Malchiram, Amram and Jehoram (with Joram), following the practice of filing a compound name under its second element. Adoniram stays in names/adoniram.json under adon (its note says no רום entry existed; it could now point here). Not written: Hiram/Huram (חִירָם), whose tie to אֲחִירָם is not shown; Jeremiah, Jeremoth/Jerimoth, Ramiah, Meremoth and Shemiramoth, which may be of רום or of רמה and are not clear. Peshitta: the brief found no root; the words were taken from SEDRA root 1745 (ܪܡ) through the database's nt_word; pointing of the Syriac lemmas follows the database's vocalised forms; a pael at Heb 7:26 (וַמרַיַמ) is not entered. Arabic روم “seek, desire” (Lane p. 1193) does not share the meaning and is not recorded; Nöldeke's pairing of رام يروم with رام يريم is a lead only. Akkadian: no cognate found (Oracc's ramû “settle”, “slacken” are other roots; Wiktionary's ramûm was not traced to a text). Not consulted: Dillmann and Leslau for Geʿez (gez-rayama rests on the root-set data), DULAT, CAL, Payne Smith. Open questions: (1) whether רָמוּת (Ezk 32:5) is “height/heap” or something else; (2) whether the hiphil's “lift off, set apart” and Arabic rāma yarīmu “depart” / Sabaic “take away” are one older sense or two; (3) the doctrine items holy-contribution-of-the-land and crown-removed-until-he-comes are written in the user's reading of Ezekiel and the kingdom; (4) Act 1:6–7 is read as Jesus answering only the time.
